translations.source_sense_description: соединяя, добавлять к чему-либо, делать частью чего-либо

glosses: To connect or combine into one; to put together.

examples.text: The plumber joined the two ends of the broken pipe.
We joined our efforts to get an even better result.

glosses: To come together; to meet.

examples.text: Parallel lines never join.
These two rivers join in about 80 miles.

glosses: To enter into association or alliance, to unite in a common purpose.

examples.text:
Forſake thy king and do but ioyne with me
And we will triumph ouer al the world.
[…]Nature and Fortune ioyn’d to make thee great.

glosses: To come into the company of.

examples.text: I will join you watching the football game as soon as I have finished my work.

No matter how early I came down, I would find him on the veranda, smoking cigarettes, or otherwise his man would be there with a message to say that his master would shortly join me if I would kindly wait.

glosses: To become a member of.

examples.text: Many children join a sports club.
Most politicians have joined a party.

In the autumn there was a row at some cement works about the unskilled labour men. A union had just been started for them and all but a few joined. One of these blacklegs was laid for by a picket and knocked out of time.

glosses: To produce an intersection of data in two or more database tables.

examples.text: By joining the Customer table on the Product table, we can show each customer's name alongside the products they have ordered.

glosses: To unite in marriage.

examples.text: Into the whiche holy eſtate theſe two perſones pꝛeſent: come nowe to be ioyned.

[…]this fellow wil but ioyne you together, as they ioyne
 Wainscot, then one of you wil proue a ſhrunke pannell[…]
What therefore God hath ioyned together, let not man put aſunder.

glosses: To enjoin upon; to command.

examples.text: And they ioyne them penaunce / as they call it / to faſt / to goo pylgremages ⁊ geve ſo moch to make ſatiſfaccion with all.

glosses: To accept, or engage in, as a contest.

examples.text: to join encounter, battle, or issue

Then when our powers in points of ſwords are ioin’d
And cloſde in compaſſe of the killing bullet, […]
On the rough edge of battel ere it joyn'd.
Before joining battle, the officers and warriors gathered to make divinations "before the spirits of the former rulers," as at the battle of Yen-ling between Chin and Ch'u in 575 b.c.

glosses: An act of joining or the state of being joined; a junction or joining.

examples.text: We found 217 putative interchromosomal joins. Only one of these joins (in the paternal assembly of HG02080) was located in a euchromatic, non-acrocentric region and was manually confirmed to be a misassembly.

glosses: An intersection of piping or wiring; an interconnect.
An intersection of data in two or more database tables.
The act of joining something, such as a network.

examples.text: The offline domain join is a three-step process described subsequently: […]

glosses: The lowest upper bound, an operation between pairs of elements in a lattice, denoted by the symbol ∨.

glosses: To hang or attach to, as by a string, so that the thing is suspended

examples.text: a seal appended to a record
An inscription was appended to the column.

glosses: To add, as an accessory to the principal thing; to annex

examples.text: notes appended to a book chapter

glosses: To write more data to the end of a pre-existing file, string, or other object.
An instance of writing more data to the end of an existing file.

examples.text: After recursively sorting the two subsets, the situation is (11,28) 35 (45,50,62) and an append of the three pieces gives the final result.
Logging can be used to back out bad data, be it an overwrite of existing data or an append of new data.
When a file is created or expanded due to an append of new data to the file, new blocks are allocated to the file.

translations.source_sense_description: соединяя, добавлять к чему-либо, делать частью чего-либо

glosses: A bound morpheme added to a word’s stem, such as a prefix or suffix.

examples.text: A prefix is an affix that joins to the beginning of another word. Depending on the prefix, it can slightly or significantly alter the meaning of a word. For example, the English prefix “un-” changes a word into its opposite, as from “do” to “undo,” altering its meaning entirely.

glosses: That which is affixed; an appendage.
The complex number a+bi associated with the point in the Gauss plane with coordinates (a,b).
Any small feature, as a figure, a flower, or the like, added for ornament to a vessel or other utensil, to an architectural feature.
To attach.

examples.text: to affix a stigma to a person
to affix ridicule or blame to somebody
Should they [caterpillars] affix them to the leaves of a plant improper for their food […]

glosses: To subjoin, annex, or add at the close or end; to append to.

examples.text: to affix a syllable to a word
to affix a seal to an instrument
to affix one’s name to a writing

glosses: To fix or fasten figuratively; with on or upon.

examples.text: eyes affixed upon the ground
Look thou no further, but affix thine eye/On that bright, shiny, round, still moving mass,/The house of blessed gods, which men call sky,/All sow'd with glist'ring stars more thick than grass...

translations.source_sense_description: соединяя, добавлять к чему-либо, делать частью чего-либо

glosses: To fasten, to join to (literally and figuratively).

examples.text: You need to attach the carabiner to your harness.
An officer is attached to a certain regiment, company, or ship.
The shoulder blade is […] attached only to the muscles.
A huge stone, to which the cable on the left bank was attached, was removed years later

Turbines have been around for a long time—windmills and water wheels are early examples. The name comes from the Latin turbo, meaning vortex, and thus the defining property of a turbine is that a fluid or gas turns the blades of a rotor, which is attached to a shaft that can perform useful work.

glosses: To adhere; to be attached.

examples.text: The great interest which attaches to the mere knowledge of these facts cannot be doubted.

glosses: To include an attachment with a communication (especially an email or other electronic communication).

examples.text: I've attached the contract to this email.

glosses: To come into legal operation in connection with anything; to vest.

examples.text: Dower will attach.
it therefore becomes important to know at what time the lien for taxes will attach.

glosses: To win the heart of; to connect by ties of love or self-interest; to attract; to fasten or bind by moral influence; with to.

examples.text: incapable of attaching a sensible man
God […] by various ties attaches man to man.
attached to a friend; attaching others to us by wealth or flattery

glosses: To connect, in a figurative sense; to ascribe or attribute; to affix; with to.

examples.text: to attach great importance to a particular circumstance
To this treasure a curse is attached.

glosses: To take, seize, or lay hold of.

examples.text: Then homeward every man attach the hand / Of his fair mistress.

glosses: To arrest, seize.

examples.text: Eftsoones the Gard, which on his state did wait, / Attacht that faitor false, and bound him strait […]
Old lord, I cannot blame thee, / Who am myself attach'd with weariness / To th' dulling of my spirits: sit down, and rest.
The earl marshal attached Gloucester for high treason.

glosses: To include (something) as a part.

examples.text: The design of his house incorporates a spiral staircase.
to incorporate another's ideas into one's work
The Romans[…] did not subdue a country in order to put the inhabitants to fire and sword, but to incorporate them into their own community.

In spite of their small size and low weight, many technical developments which have proved themselves in main-line service have been incorporated, and a novelty in the 2-6-0-type is a tender cab to improve the conditions of tender-first running.

The new cars incorporate many features first introduced in the 1938 tube stock, but major changes include the use of rubber for the bogie bolster and axlebox suspension, fluorescent lighting, and the panelling of the cars in unpainted aluminium alloy.

So what is it that makes SBB (Swiss national railways) tick? In my humble opinion, two things. Firstly, a comprehensive and set-in-stone integrated timetable (incorporating trains, ferries, cable cars and buses, including the world-famous yellow 'post-autos'), compiled four years in advance and which gets tested twice before it becomes operational.

glosses: To mix (something in) as an ingredient; to blend

examples.text: Incorporate air into the mixture by whisking.

glosses: To admit as a member of a company
To form into a legal company.

examples.text: The company was incorporated in 1980.

glosses: To include (another clause or guarantee of the US constitution) as a part (of the Fourteenth Amendment, such that the clause binds not only the federal government but also state governments).
To form into a body; to combine, as different ingredients, into one consistent mass.

examples.text: By your leaves, you shall not stay alone, / Till holy church incorporate two in one.

glosses: To unite with a material body; to give a material form to; to embody.

examples.text: do not deny , that there was such an Opinion among the Heathens , that Spirits might possess Images , and be incorporated with them

glosses: Corporate; incorporated; made one body, or united in one body; associated; mixed together; combined; embodied.

examples.text: As if our hands, our sides, voices, and minds / Had been incorporate.
a fifteenth part of silver incorporate with gold

And gazing on thee, sullen tree,
⁠Sick for thy stubborn hardihood,
⁠I seem to fail from out my blood
And grow incorporate into thee.

glosses: Not consisting of matter; not having a material body; incorporeal; spiritual.

examples.text: Moses forbore to speak of angels, and of things invisible, and incorporate.

The air vibrated at a white-hot temperature, the stones seemed to be trembling silently, ready to flow, and in the distance, at a curve of the road, the files of men, guns and horses seemed detached from the earth, and trembled like a mass of jelly in their onward progress, and it seemed to me that they were not living people that I saw before me, but an army of incorporate shadows.

glosses: Not incorporated; not existing as a corporation.
